title: Static Routing Configuration in GNS3 (Router & Host Setup)
description: Complete Cisco IOS and VPCS terminal configuration commands for setting up static routes across R1 and R2 routers in a GNS3 network topology.
aim: To configure and verify Static Routing between two Cisco routers connecting distinct subnets using GNS3.
theory: Static routing is a method where routes are manually programmed into a router's routing table using the 'ip route <destination-network> <subnet-mask> <next-hop-ip>' command. Unlike dynamic routing protocols, static routes do not incur bandwidth or CPU overhead and provide predictable deterministic packet paths. In this GNS3 topology (PC1 - Switch1 - R1 - R2 - Switch2 - PC2), R1 is configured with a static route to the 192.168.3.0/24 subnet via R2 (192.168.2.2), and R2 with a static route to the 192.168.1.0/24 subnet via R1 (192.168.2.1), enabling bidirectional ICMP echo ping communication.
algorithm: Configure host IP, subnet mask, and default gateway on PC1 (192.168.1.2/24 -> gateway 192.168.1.1).
On R1, configure FastEthernet 0/0 (192.168.1.1/24) and FastEthernet 1/0 (192.168.2.1/24) interfaces with 'no shutdown'.
On R2, configure FastEthernet 1/0 (192.168.2.2/24) and FastEthernet 0/0 (192.168.3.1/24) interfaces with 'no shutdown'.
Configure host IP, subnet mask, and default gateway on PC2 (192.168.3.2/24 -> gateway 192.168.3.1).
Verify interfaces using 'show ip interface brief' and routing table using 'show ip route'.
Test end-to-end connectivity by pinging PC2 from PC1 (ping 192.168.3.2) and vice-versa.
